items.author: Joe Hudson
items.text:
The next time you notice yourself judging someone, pause and ask:

“What am I trying not to feel right now?”

Bonus version: Also do this when you notice that you're judging yourself.

items.author: Chris Williamson
items.text:
“Cynicism in relationships is a defence against heartbreak and betrayal, and it's very effective at that.
The trouble is when you get so good at it that you accidentally defend yourself from ever falling in love.” - Mark Ryan

Cynicism is a guarded response which sets yourself up against disappointment.

Its role within the system is to protect you against experiencing anything bad. It is a pre-emptive strike against a perceived threat.

If I tell myself that 'all women are bad', then I'm less likely to seek a relationship and, as a consequence, I'm never going to feel the pain of rejection.

If I tell myself that 'everything is shit' or that 'things will never get better', then I am excused of ever having to try at anything.

It's more comfortable to get fatalistic and call it pragmatism.

The cope is framing hope as pathetic and embarrassing and optimism as delusion.

The upside of never trying is never having to feel the pain of failure.

And it’s a devil’s bargain.

items.author: Santa Carota Beef
items.text:
Weekend Prayer 🧡

Heavenly Father, as another week comes to a close, we thank You for the blessings we’ve received, the challenges You’ve helped us through, and the prayers You continue to hear.

We ask that You bring peace to those carrying worries into the weekend, strength to those facing difficult seasons, and comfort to those who need a little extra grace. Help us appreciate what we have today without losing faith in what tomorrow may bring.

Watch over our families, our livestock, our land, and all those working to provide for others. May the weekend bring a little rest, time with loved ones, and a reminder of Your goodness through every season.

In Jesus’ name, Amen.

items.author: Preethi Kasireddy
items.text:
You'd think by kid number 3 I'd have learned that when a toddler goes quiet for more than a couple minutes, they're up to no good.

And still, this morning my 11 month old went quiet while I was getting ready and I thought, I'll just finish real quick.

Found him happily petting the toilet brush with his hands 😭
